IF YOU WANT TO WRITE SQL LIKE A SENIOR ENGINEER, STOP SELECTING STAR.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES:

Name your columns, always.

SELECT * breaks when schemas change and drags dead weight over the wire. Explicit beats lazy.

Filter early with WHERE, not HAVING.

WHERE cuts rows before grouping. HAVING cuts after. Same result, wildly different cost.

Index what you filter and join.

Check EXPLAIN before and after. One composite index has saved more weekends than any ORM.

IF YOU WANT QUERIES THAT SCALE PAST A MILLION ROWS, STOP NESTING SUBQUERIES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 MOVES:

JOIN beats subquery in the SELECT list.

Correlated subqueries run once per row. A JOIN runs once. Measure it and weep.

CTEs for readability, temp tables for size.

WITH makes logic clear. Past six figures of rows, materialize and index instead.

Paginate with keyset, not OFFSET.

WHERE id > last_id LIMIT 100 stays fast on page 10,000. OFFSET rescans everything.

IF YOU WANT TO DEBUG SLOW QUERIES FAST, STOP GUESSING.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 CHECKS:

Run EXPLAIN first, always.

Seq scan on a big table is your prime suspect. The plan tells you where time goes.

Check for missing indexes on JOIN keys.

Unindexed foreign keys turn joins into nested loops from hell.

Watch for N+1 hiding in ORMs.

One query per parent plus one per child. Eager load or batch it and watch latency collapse.
